demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.heading: On your lane: hold a fault, read the plan, run it by hand
demos.purpose: make remediate OFFLINE=1 reads the kit's own recording of this drill, ops/incidents/held_model.json. It needs no PROJECT and no credential, and it prints the plan you should get on the lane, with your lane's revision names in place of these. HOLD=1 writes deploy/.fault-hold first, with the variable as it was and the revision serving, so that RESTORE=1 always has a record. Then it sets the fault, and the new revision takes the traffic. It runs the smoke once, so that the lane holds the fault's own turns for remediate to read, and it leaves the fault in place. remediate reads the lane three times and prints the plan. SAVE= keeps what it read, with the project id and number replaced, so the incident can be replayed later. Expect bad_revision, the change CHAT_MODEL: unset -> "gemini-3.6-flsh", and a rollback to the revision HOLD=1 recorded as serving before the fault. Paste step 1's command as your plan printed it, or set PREV to the revision it names. It moves traffic only: the fault's revision stays, at 0%. The plan's step 2. Every brain should answer, because the traffic is on the revision before the fault. Expect rolled_back. The plan starts again from the verify, and does not print the rollback a second time: its step 1 says the rollback is done.

steps.expected:
remediate: documind-chat on documind-ai-YOUR-ID (us-central1), the 60 minutes to 2026-10-12 10:00 UTC (15:30 IST)
rules only: no model is called, and nothing on the lane is changed.
read from a recorded state: held_model.json (make incident-drill FAULT=model HOLD=1 and its smoke: CHAT_MODEL=gemini-3.6-flsh, a mistyped model, fails every agent turn with a 500)

What the lane shows
  traffic     100% documind-chat-00042-tvd (following the latest revision)
  revision    documind-chat-00042-tvd  created 2026-10-12 09:41 UTC (15:11 IST), inside the window  [serving]
  revision    documind-chat-00041-kpw  created 2026-10-09 06:12 UTC (11:42 IST)  [the revision before it]
  the change  CHAT_MODEL: unset -> "gemini-3.6-flsh"
  answers     documind-chat-00042-tvd: 5 requests, 3 answered 5xx (60%); 1 chat turn, 0 stopped by a limit
  answers     documind-chat-00041-kpw: nothing in the window
  signal      5xx answers, silent: no alert policy the kit declares counts a service's 5xx answers

Diagnosis - rule bad_revision
  documind-chat-00042-tvd was created inside the window and fails (5xx answers); documind-chat-00041-kpw, the revision
  before it, answered nothing in the window, so it shows no failure. Between the two, only CHAT_MODEL changed.

The plan. remediate runs none of it: you do, in this order.
  1. Roll back: all traffic to documind-chat-00041-kpw, which never went away (documind-chat-00042-tvd stays, at 0%).
       gcloud run services update-traffic documind-chat --region us-central1 --project documind-ai-YOUR-ID --to-revisions documind-chat-00041-kpw=100
  2. Verify: every brain answers.
       make smoke-chat PROJECT=documind-ai-YOUR-ID REGION=us-central1
  3. Restore. The rollback moved traffic only: the template still carries the change, and a service whose traffic is
     pinned to a revision by name leaves every later revision at 0%. Undo the change, then send the traffic to the
     latest revision, in that order (the other order sends it back to documind-chat-00042-tvd).
       gcloud run services update documind-chat --region us-central1 --project documind-ai-YOUR-ID --remove-env-vars=CHAT_MODEL --quiet
       gcloud run services update-traffic documind-chat --region us-central1 --project documind-ai-YOUR-ID --to-latest
     This checkout holds the drill's fault (deploy/.fault-hold): make incident-drill RESTORE=1
     PROJECT=documind-ai-YOUR-ID runs both.
  4. Verify again: make smoke-chat PROJECT=documind-ai-YOUR-ID REGION=us-central1, then make remediate
     PROJECT=documind-ai-YOUR-ID SERVICE=documind-chat: it reads no failure.

0 model calls. Nothing on the lane was changed.

demos.heading: Architecture: the path an incident takes, read by read and rule by rule
demos.purpose: The loop runs make remediate OFFLINE=1 on each of the kit's seven recordings and prints, for each, the rule that decided, how many commands the plan printed, and its last line. The cell loads remediate.py, prints the only commands it may run, the events it reads on each service, the exact filter of its one logging read for the drill's window, and holds five commands against the denylist. RUNBOOKS=1 lists every policy the kit declares with its runbook and what remediate may do. Its first line, and the two signals no policy watches: One GET on the Monitoring API lists every alert policy on your lane by its display name, and the cell holds each against ops/runbooks.json. On a lane deployed with the defaults, expect eleven: three that remediate may roll back for and eight that are a person's, with the other six behind their switches. A no row line would be a policy that pages with no runbook remediate knows.
